To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of papers use data collected from GitHub (90%), the majority of papers are based on the analysis of one or two datasets (60%) and that most of them do not report any limitation (60%).

(1) most of the research papers in the field use a single dataset, which is not always available to the public, (2) the most popular dataset, which is available to the public and is the one used by most research papers, is the one collected by Gousios et al., (3) the most popular empirical method is to use the Gousios dataset and apply a statistical analysis to it, (4) the most popular statistical analysis method is to apply regression, (

1) most of the papers use the GitHub API to collect data, 2) most of the datasets used are small, 3) the most used sampling technique is the random sampling, 4) the most used empirical method is the case study, 5) the most used data analysis technique is the statistical analysis, 6) most of the research papers do not report limitations and, when reporting, most of the limitations are related to the data collection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of the empirical research performed on GitHub.
the reproducibility and replicability of the results of research papers that use GitHub as a dataset source.
the reproducibility and replicability of research papers based on GitHub data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art of mining GitHub data is not yet ready for a large-scale replication of findings.
the current research community is not yet ready for large-scale empirical studies on GitHub.
the current state of the practice is not mature enough to be used as reference to draw generalizable conclusions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the research community is aware of the importance of reporting the limitations and the dataset collection process, the current practice is not yet at the level required to guarantee replicability and to avoid the use of biased datasets.
the community has been using GitHub to mine data for research purposes, but it has done so without a clear understanding of what is being done and how to do it better.
there is still a lot of room for improving how we conduct research based on GitHub repositories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the large amount of research papers that have been published, there is a lack of a common ground for mining GitHub data.
, while the community has been able to learn a lot from GitHub, we still need to improve in terms of research methods and reporting.
the research community needs to pay more attention to the research process, including data collection, data cleaning, and replication.
